slides.reveal: Answer: B. Water vapor and carbon dioxide low in the atmosphere absorb most infrared (slide 12; OpenStax 5.2, 6.5), and an infrared telescope must be very cold so it does not glow in the light it is trying to see; at L2 Webb's sunshield keeps it under 50 K (slide 13; NASA Webb Fact Sheet; OpenStax 6.5).

Two stars have the same luminosity. Star Y is 3 times farther away. How bright does Y look?

slides.reveal: Answer: B. Brightness falls with the square of the distance: 3 times farther spreads the light over 3² = 9 times the area, so Y looks 1/9 as bright (slide 16; OpenStax 17.1: 'three times farther away, it will look nine (three squared) times dimmer').
